one_line: Anonymous South Indian crucible steel maker from Kodumanal linked to Indian Ocean trade, c. 500 BCE–300 CE.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, lean and muscular from forge work, average height with solid shoulders.
appearance.face: Oval face, medium-brown South Indian complexion, straight nose, strong jaw, faint soot smudges on cheeks, a small healed burn-scar near left temple, default expression focused and calm with sharp, observant eyes.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair pulled into a short, neat back knot at the nape (no topknot), front slightly tousled; simple narrow cloth headband in deep indigo wrapped low across the forehead to keep sweat from the eyes.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate South Indian working attire: a knee-length off-white cotton tunic (similar to a simple anga) with short sleeves, slightly loose but tied close with a narrow reddish-brown woven waist sash; below, a mid-calf-length unbleached cotton veshti/dhoti wrapped securely, pleated in front and allowing free movement; dark brown leather sandals with simple straps; minimal jewellery—a thin copper bangle on the right wrist and small plain copper ear studs; fabrics are matte and slightly smoke-stained, with the tunic showing subtle vertical weave lines and the sash bearing a faint, simple geometric border pattern.
appearance.signature: A clay crucible for wootz-making held carefully in one hand, rounded and slightly tapered with a sealed clay lid and faint soot-darkening, and in the other a long iron tongs tool used to handle the hot crucibles.

ref_desc: A lean mid-30s South Indian ironworker with medium-brown skin, back-knotted black hair and indigo headband, wearing an off-white tunic, unbleached veshti, reddish-brown sash and dark brown sandals, carrying a soot-darkened sealed clay crucible with long iron tongs.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style South Indian ironworker from c. 500 BCE–300 CE exactly as follows: a lean, muscular man in his mid-30s with medium-brown Tamil complexion, oval face, straight nose, strong jaw, faint soot smudges on his cheeks and a small healed burn-scar near his left temple, eyes sharp and calmly focused. His thick black hair is pulled into a short, neat knot at the back of his neck, with a narrow deep indigo cloth headband wrapped low across his forehead to keep sweat out of his eyes. He wears an era-accurate off-white cotton tunic with short sleeves and subtle vertical weave lines, hanging to just below the hips and cinched firmly with a narrow reddish-brown woven waist sash that has a faint geometric border; below, a mid-calf-length unbleached cotton veshti/dhoti is wrapped and pleated in front in a practical working style. On his feet are simple dark brown leather sandals with plain straps. His only jewellery is a thin copper bangle on his right wrist and small plain copper ear studs, both slightly dulled from forge work. In his right hand he carefully holds a rounded, slightly tapered clay crucible with a sealed clay lid and soot-darkened sides, and in his left hand he grips a long iron tongs tool used to handle hot crucibles. Use a palette dominated by off-white for the tunic, unbleached cream for the veshti, deep indigo for the headband, reddish-brown for the sash, and dark brown for the sandals and iron tools, with overall subtle smoke-staining to suggest the forge environment; show him standing in a neutral pose that clearly exposes his face, hair, full costume head-to-toe, crucible and tongs.
